spec.description: Cancels multiple orders (minimum 2, maximum 50) in a single request, identified by a mix of client or Kraken identifiers.

request.title: BatchCancelParams
request.description: Parameters for cancelling multiple orders (minimum 2, maximum 50) in a single request, identified by a mix of client or Kraken identifiers.

orders.title: OrderReferenceList
orders.description: List containing either client `order_userref` or Kraken `order_id` identifiers, 2 to 50 of them.

response.title: BatchCancelReply
response.description: Reply to a `batch_cancel` request -- the count lives directly on the frame, not under a `result` key.

orders_cancelled.description: Number of orders cancelled. Confirmed live -- upstream's docs page instead describes a nested `result: {count, warnings}` shape, which the real reply does not send; see `notes`.

warnings.description: Non-fatal warnings about the cancellation, if any. Documented by upstream nested under `result`; kept top-level here to match the real reply's flat shape, unconfirmed live (none appeared in this run's capture).

notes: `token` (the auth bearer token) is documented by Kraken as a required params field but is deliberately absent from this schema: `core/transport/ws.py`'s `SocketConnection.rpc_send` merges the cached token into every outgoing `params` on the private connection -- trading calls and subscribe/unsubscribe alike -- so it is transport-injected, never a caller-supplied argument, the same way `req_id` (the declared `correlate` field) never appears in a requestBody schema. `orders` (order_userref or order_id, mixed) and `cl_ord_id` are two separate identifier lists, both documented as usable in the same request (unlike `cancel_order`'s mutually-exclusive identifier fields), so both are kept as independent array properties.

CONFIRMED LIVE, CORE-LEVEL FINDING: unlike every other WS trading command in this subsection, `batch_cancel`'s real reply does not nest its payload under `result` -- a real capture returned `{'method': 'batch_cancel', 'orders_cancelled': 2, 'req_id': 4, 'success': True, 'time_in': ..., 'time_out': ...}`, with no `result` key at all, contradicting upstream's own docs page (which describes `result: {count, warnings}`). Consequently no `envelope` is declared here, and the response schema describes the whole frame. This means `core/transport/ws.py`'s `KrakenSocketClient.request()`, which unconditionally does `reply.get('result')`, would silently return `None` for a real `batch_cancel` call today instead of the real cancellation count -- a genuine core bug distinct from this spec fix, since the core's generic extraction assumes every WS command nests under `result`, which is true for the other 7 commands in this subsection but not this one. Needs a core-level special case (e.g. an endpoint-aware unwrap, or codegen honoring the per-endpoint `envelope` declaration precisely) before `trading_ws.batch_cancel` returns useful data through the hand-written core as it stands.
